title: Female borrowers who mention sustaining their business specifically through NWTF loans may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who include their specific age in the pitch may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who include the loan amount in local currency may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention longer periods of business experience may fund faster.
Female borrowers who explicitly state their confidence or ability to repay the loan may fund faster.
Female borrowers who link the loan to community wellbeing or family care may fund faster.
Female borrowers who include explicit expressions of gratitude to lenders or partners may fund faster.
Female borrowers who include detailed descriptions of local geography or tourism may fund faster.
Female borrowers who provide specific details about their training may fund faster.
Mentioning specific marital status or lack of dependents may predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Mentioning the education of children predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention their past loan repayment history fund faster.
Female borrowers who list a wide variety of specific inventory items fund faster.
